# Remote Project Kickoff Plan for 3 June 2026

A focused 45-minute kickoff works best with tight timeboxes, clear owners, and one decision point per agenda item. This structure keeps product, design, and engineering aligned without overrunning.

## 45-Minute Meeting Agenda

| Time | Topic | Lead | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14:00–14:05 | Welcome and objectives | Facilitator | Confirm purpose, scope, and meeting goals |
| 14:05–14:12 | Project goals | Product lead | Align on success criteria and priorities |
| 14:12–14:22 | Timeline and milestones | Project lead | Confirm phases, dependencies, and key dates |
| 14:22–14:32 | Risks and blockers | Engineering lead | Surface top risks, assumptions, and mitigations |
| 14:32–14:40 | Next steps and ownership | Facilitator | Assign action items, owners, and due dates |
| 14:40–14:45 | Wrap-up and recap | Facilitator | Restate decisions and confirm follow-up |

## Suggested Meeting Flow

- Keep introductions to 1 minute per person or skip them if the group already knows each other.
- Use the timeline segment to confirm what is fixed vs. flexible.
- Capture risks live in a shared note with an owner beside each risk.
- End with explicit next steps, not just discussion notes.

## Follow-Up Email Template

**Subject:** Kickoff recap and next steps — Project meeting on 3 June 2026

Hi team,

Thanks for joining the kickoff today. We aligned on the project goals, reviewed the timeline, discussed key risks, and confirmed the next steps.

**Key takeaways**
- Project goal: [insert agreed goal]
- Timeline: [insert major milestone dates]
- Top risks: [insert 1–3 risks]
- Decisions made: [insert key decisions]

**Action items**
- [Owner name] — [Action item 1] — Due: [date]
- [Owner name] — [Action item 2] — Due: [date]
- [Owner name] — [Action item 3] — Due: [date]
- [Owner name] — [Action item 4] — Due: [date]

Please reply if I missed anything or if any owner/due date needs updating.

Best,
[Your name]
